messages.author: 31d6f47354d13cb1
messages.subject: ask for help in lavaan
parts:
Hello,

I have a question about a multi-group confirmatory factor analysis in R with the package lavaan and would be very happy to receive an answer.
 I have imported my data set into R. It contains the variable "minispin_screening", which can have the values 0 or 1 (nominally scaled) with the values having the following correspondences:
0 = negative
1 = positive.

I want to perform a multi-group CFA in lavaan and have used the following script:

 
library(lavaan)

data(dataset_all)
levels(dataset_all$minispin_screening)

model1 <- '
autonomy_sat =~ s_bpnsfs01 + s_bpnsfs07 + s_bpnsfs13 + s_bpnsfs19
autonomy_frust =~ s_bpnsfs02 + s_bpnsfs08 + s_bpnsfs14 + s_bpnsfs20
relatedness_sat =~ s_bpnsfs03 + s_bpnsfs09 + s_bpnsfs15 + s_bpnsfs21
relatedness_frust =~ s_bpnsfs04 + s_bpnsfs10 + s_bpnsfs16 + s_bpnsfs22
competence_sat =~ s_bpnsfs05 + s_bpnsfs11 + s_bpnsfs17 + s_bpnsfs23
competence_frust =~ s_bpnsfs06 + s_bpnsfs12 + s_bpnsfs18 + s_bpnsfs24
'

fit1 <- cfa(model1,
            data = dataset_all,
            group = "minispin_screening",
            std.lv = TRUE)

summary(fit1, fit.measures =TRUE, standardized = TRUE)


I get the following error messages:
> levels(dataset_all$minispin_screening)
NULL

> fit1 <- cfa(model = model1,
+ data = dataset_all,
+ group = "minispin_screening",
+ std.lv = TRUE)
Error in `vec_equal()`:
! Can't combine `..1` <character> and `..2` <double>.
Run `rlang::last_trace()` to see where the error occurred.

 and no results are returned. I've been looking for the error for days, but can't find it. The variable to be grouped is actually nominally scaled with 2 values, as in the example data set (HolzingerSwineford1929).

Can you help me with this? Thank you very much in advance.

Yours sincerely
Felicitas Posch

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: ask for help in lavaan
parts:
Have you run the following as suggested?

rlang::last_trace()

You can also run this:

traceback()

Run the above call right after you see the error message, that is, right after you run cfa().

If possible, post the output of last_trace() or traceback() here can help identifying the source of the problem.

You can also run the following:

fit1 <- cfa(model1,
            data = dataset_all,

std.lv = TRUE)

Run the above lines to see whethe the error was due to grouping. If the error still occurred, then it is not about the grouping but about something else.

By the way, install the latest version of lavaan (0.6-18) if you have not yet done so.

-- Shu Fai

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: ask for help in lavaan
parts:
Maybe you have another function called 'cfa()' in your workspace. Try
using lavaan::cfa().

In any case, 'vec_equal()' is not a lavaan function, and lavaan does not
use rlang.

Yves.
